title: Rotational dynamics
competency: Define torque and moment of inertia and use τ = Iα with the rotation equations.

keywords.def: The turning effect of a force: τ = rF sinθ, in N m.
A body's resistance to change in its rotation: I = Σmr², in kg m².
The sum of all torques on a body, counterclockwise positive: τ_net = Iα.

en.text: Torque is the turning effect of a force: τ = rF sinθ, where r is the distance from the axis to the force and θ is the angle between r and F. Its unit is N m. Counterclockwise torques are usually positive, clockwise negative; the direction follows the right-hand rule.

am.text: ቶርክ የኃይል የማዞር ውጤት ነው፡ τ = rF sinθ (N m)። ከሰዓት ተቃራኒ አቅጣጫ አዎንታዊ፣ በሰዓት አቅጣጫ አሉታዊ ነው።

screens.title: Door handles
screens.ask: Why is a door handle put far from the hinges?
opts: The same push turns the door more easily
screens.after:
A force far from the hinges has a bigger turning effect.
Torque τ = rF sinθ grows with r.
So the same push turns the door more easily.
screens.best: The same push turns the door more easily

screens.title: Torque
paras: Torque makes a body gain angular acceleration.
r: distance from the axis to where the force acts.
θ: angle between r and F, drawn from the same point.
Unit: N m. Torque is a vector along the axis (right-hand rule).

screens.title: Turn a spanner
screens.ask: Change the distance, the force and the angle. When is the torque largest? When is it zero?
screens.note: Largest at θ = 90°. Zero at 0° and 180°: the force points along the spanner.

screens.title: Key word
defs: The turning effect of a force: τ = rF sinθ, in N m.

screens.text: Torque and angle: a force pushes straight along a rod toward its pivot (θ = 0°). The torque is
screens.why:
Formula: τ = rF sinθ.
θ = 0°, and sin0° = 0.
So τ = rF × 0 = 0.
A push along the rod cannot turn it.

screens.ask: Torque: a 400 N force acts 5 m from a pivot at 30° to the beam. τ = ___ N m
screens.why:
Formula: τ = rF sinθ.
Substitute: τ = 5 m × 400 N × sin30°.
sin30° = 0.5, so τ = 2000 × 0.5.
Result: τ = 1000 N m.
Trap: using cos30° gives 1732 N m.
screens.clue: Use sinθ with the angle between beam and force.

screens.ask: Torque at an obtuse angle: a 16 N force acts 4.0 m from O at 150° to r. τ = ___ N m
screens.why:
Formula: τ = rF sinθ.
sin150° = sin30° = 0.5.
τ = 4.0 × 16 × 0.5 = 32 N m.
It turns counterclockwise, so it is +32 N m.

screens.ask: Net torque: three torques act on a rod pivoted at O: −26.0 N m (clockwise), +32 N m and +107.5 N m. τ_net = ___ N m (1 decimal place)
screens.why:
Counterclockwise is +, clockwise is −.
τ_net = −26.0 + 32 + 107.5.
Result: τ_net = 113.5 N m.
Positive, so the net turning is counterclockwise.

screens.ask: Net torque from three forces: F₁ = 10 N at 3.0 m and 120° (clockwise), F₂ = 16 N at 4.0 m and 150°, F₃ = 19 N at 8.0 m and 45° (both counterclockwise). τ_net ≈ ___ N m (1 decimal place)
screens.clue: Work out each torque, give it a sign, then add.

en.text: Moment of inertia measures how hard it is to change a body's rotation. For a point mass, I = mr²; for several masses, I = m₁r₁² + m₂r₂² + … . Its unit is kg m² and it is a scalar. It depends on the mass and on where the mass sits relative to the axis.

am.text: የማዞር ኢነርሺያ መዞርን ለመለወጥ ያለውን ተቃውሞ ይለካል፡ I = Σmr² (kg m²)። በብዛቱና ከዘንጉ ባለው ርቀት ይወሰናል።

screens.title: Which spins more easily?
screens.ask: Two equal rods carry the same two masses. On rod A the masses are at the ends; on rod B they are near the middle. Which is easier to start spinning about its centre?
screens.after:
Moment of inertia I = Σmr².
On rod B the masses are near the axis: small r, small mr².
So rod B resists turning less and is easier to spin.

screens.title: Moment of inertia
paras: Mass resists changes in linear motion.
Moment of inertia I resists changes in rotation.
Several masses: I = m₁r₁² + m₂r₂² + m₃r₃² + …
Unit: kg m². It is a scalar.
It depends on the mass and on the axis.

screens.title: Where the mass sits
screens.ask: Move the mass away from the axis. Watch I.
screens.note: Doubling m doubles I. Doubling r makes I four times larger.

screens.title: Key word
defs: A body's resistance to change in its rotation: I = Σmr², in kg m².

screens.text: Units: the SI unit of moment of inertia is
screens.why:
Formula: I = mr².
Units: kg × m × m = kg m².
Trap: N m is torque; kg m/s is momentum.
screens.clue: Look at the formula I = mr².

screens.ask: Moment of inertia of a point mass: a 2 kg mass turns 0.5 m from the axis. I = ___ kg m²
screens.why:
Formula: I = mr².
Square r first: 0.5² = 0.25 m².
I = 2 kg × 0.25 m² = 0.5 kg m².
Trap: 2 × 0.5 = 1 forgets to square r.

screens.ask: Moment of inertia of several masses: 4 kg, 2 kg and 3 kg sit 3 m, 2 m and 4 m from the axis. I = ___ kg m²
screens.why:
Formula: I = m₁r₁² + m₂r₂² + m₃r₃².
4 × 3² = 36; 2 × 2² = 8; 3 × 4² = 48.
I = 36 + 8 + 48 = 92 kg m².
(The book prints 164; 92 is correct.)

screens.text: Moment of inertia, true or false: moving the same masses farther from the axis makes I larger.
screens.why:
I = Σmr², and r is squared.
Larger r gives larger r².
Doubling r makes I four times larger.
So the statement is true.
screens.clue: r is squared in I = mr².

screens.text: Moment of inertia of a triangle of masses: three masses m at the corners of an equilateral triangle of side L. I about an axis through one corner, perpendicular to the triangle, is
screens.why:
The mass on the axis has r = 0, so it adds 0.
The other two masses are each a side L away.
I = mL² + mL² = 2mL².
Trap: 3mL² counts the corner mass too.
screens.clue: How far is the corner mass from the axis?

en.text: Net torque causes angular acceleration, just as net force causes linear acceleration. Newton's second law for rotation is τ_net = Iα. A bigger torque gives a bigger α; a bigger moment of inertia gives a smaller α. Then the rotation equations give ω and θ.

am.text: ጠቅላላ ቶርክ የማዕዘን ፍጥነት ለውጥ ያመጣል፡ τ = Iα። ይህ የኒውተን ሁለተኛ ሕግ ለመዞር ነው።

screens.title: Push a flywheel
screens.ask: Change the torque and the moment of inertia. Watch α.
screens.note: Double τ: α doubles. Double I: α halves. Like F = ma.

screens.title: Newton's second law for rotation
paras: Add all torques: τ_net = τ₁ + τ₂ + τ₃ + …
Linear: F = ma. Rotation: τ = Iα.
Replace m by I and a by α.
Angular acceleration is proportional to the net torque.

screens.title: Key word
defs: The sum of all torques on a body, counterclockwise positive: τ_net = Iα.

screens.text: Newton's second law for rotation: in τ = Iα, which quantity plays the part of mass?
screens.why:
Linear: F = ma.
Rotation: τ = Iα.
Force ↔ torque, acceleration ↔ angular acceleration.
So mass ↔ moment of inertia I.
screens.clue: Match F = ma letter by letter.

screens.ask: Moment of inertia from τ = Iα: a torque of 36 N m gives a wheel α = 24 rad/s². I = ___ kg m²
screens.why:
Formula: τ = Iα, so I = τ/α.
Substitute: I = 36 N m ÷ 24 rad/s².
Result: I = 1.5 kg m².

screens.ask: Angular acceleration from τ = Iα: a motor gives 100 N m to a flywheel with I = 0.1 kg m². α = ___ rad/s²
screens.why:
Formula: α = τ/I.
Substitute: α = 100 ÷ 0.1.
Result: α = 1000 rad/s².
Trap: 100 × 0.1 = 10 multiplies instead of dividing.

screens.ask: Time to reach a speed: same flywheel (α = 1000 rad/s², from rest). It reaches 150 rad/s after ___ s
screens.why:
Formula: ω_f = ω₀ + αt, with ω₀ = 0.
t = ω_f/α = 150 ÷ 1000.
Result: t = 0.15 s.

screens.ask: Torque and time: a disc (I = 2 kg m²) goes from 3 rad/s to 8 rad/s under a net torque of 50 N m. It takes ___ s
screens.why:
Step 1: α = τ/I = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 rad/s².
Step 2: t = (ω_f − ω₀)/α = (8 − 3) ÷ 25.
Result: t = 0.2 s.

test.ask: Torque: a 10 N force acts 2 m from the axis, at 90° to r. τ = ___ N m
test.why:
Formula: τ = rF sinθ.
sin90° = 1.
τ = 2 × 10 × 1 = 20 N m.

test.ask: Torque: a 40 N force acts 0.5 m from the axis, at 30° to r. τ = ___ N m
test.why:
Formula: τ = rF sinθ.
τ = 0.5 × 40 × sin30° = 20 × 0.5.
Result: 10 N m.

test.ask: Moment of inertia: a 3 kg point mass turns 2 m from the axis. I = ___ kg m²
test.why:
Formula: I = mr².
I = 3 × 2² = 3 × 4.
Result: 12 kg m².

test.ask: Angular acceleration: a net torque of 12 N m acts on a wheel with I = 4 kg m². α = ___ rad/s²
test.why:
Formula: α = τ/I.
α = 12 ÷ 4.
Result: 3 rad/s².

test.ask: Net torque: a wheel (I = 0.5 kg m²) goes from rest to 20 rad/s in 4 s. The net torque is ___ N m
test.why:
Step 1: α = Δω/Δt = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 rad/s².
Step 2: τ = Iα = 0.5 × 5.
Result: 2.5 N m.

notes.text: Example 2.14: 3 × 10 × sin120° = 25.98 ≈ 26.0 N m (book −25.9); the τ₃ line is labelled τ₂. Net torque 113.5 N m is right.
Example 2.15: 4×9 + 2×4 + 3×16 = 92 kg m², not 164. Figure 2.17 labels the distances in cm while the solution uses m; the lesson uses metres (92 kg m²). The 2 rad/s is not needed.
